\label{lem:section2-universal-obstructions}
The following statements hold.

\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If \(\be>2\d\), then \(\Pc_{\d}(\be)=+\infty\).  Equivalently, if \(A<\Acrit(\d)\), then \(\Cc_{\d}(A)=+\infty\).

\item If \(\be>\betas(\d)\), then \(\Pc_{\d}(\be)>0\).  Equivalently, if \(A<\As(\d)\), then \(\Cc_{\d}(A)>0\).
\end{enumerate}

rows.old_statement_tex:
\label{lem:circle-rearrangement}
Let $q$ be a bounded, nonnegative circle kernel that is even and
nonincreasing as a function of geodesic distance from the origin.
For nonnegative $f,g\in L^1$, let $f^*,g^*$ be their symmetric
decreasing rearrangements. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:circle-rearrangement}
 \iint f(\theta)q(\theta-\phi)g(\phi)
                  \,\dd\mu_1(\theta)\,\dd\mu_1(\phi)
 \le
 \iint f^*(\theta)q(\theta-\phi)g^*(\phi)
                  \,\dd\mu_1(\theta)\,\dd\mu_1(\phi),
\end{equation}
where $\dd\mu_1=\dd\theta/(2\pi)$. Rearrangement preserves
pointwise order and is nonexpansive in $L^1$.
rows.paper2_statement_tex:
\label{lem:circle-rearrangement}
Let $q$ be a bounded, nonnegative circle kernel that is even and
nonincreasing as a function of geodesic distance from the origin.
For nonnegative $f,g\in L^1$, let $f^*,g^*$ be their symmetric
decreasing rearrangements. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:circle-rearrangement}
 \iint f(x)q(x-y)g(y)
                  \,\dd m_1(x)\,\dd m_1(y)
 \le
 \iint f^*(x)q(x-y)g^*(y)
                  \,\dd m_1(x)\,\dd m_1(y),
\end{equation}
where $m_1$ is normalized Haar measure on $\T=\R/\Z$. 
Moreover,
\begin{equation*}
 f\le g\ \text{a.e.}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f^*\le g^*\ \text{a.e.},
 \qquad \|f^*-g^*\|_{L^1(m_1)}\le\|f-g\|_{L^1(m_1)}.
\end{equation*}

rows.old_statement_tex:
\label{lem:positive-bernstein}

Suppose $f\in C^\infty([0,1]^{\d})$ and

$\partial^\alpha f\ge0$ for every multi-index $\alpha$, including

$\alpha=0$. Then

\begin{equation}\label{eq:positive-taylor-series}
 f(y)=\sum_{\alpha\in\N_0^{\d}}c_\alpha y^\alpha,
 \qquad
 c_\alpha=\frac{\partial^\alpha f(0)}{\alpha!}\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_\alpha c_\alpha=f(1,\ldots,1),
\end{equation}

where the series converges uniformly on $[0,1]^\d$.
rows.paper2_statement_tex:

Suppose $f\in C^\infty([0,1]^{\d})$ and

 \qquad

 \qquad \sum_\alpha c_\alpha=f(1,\ldots,1),

where the series converges uniformly on $[0,1]^\d$.
